headline.question: After the Axogen–BioCircuit merger closes, Michelle Jarrard has 90 days to put together the closing balance sheet and working-capital numbers and send them to Axogen. How long does Axogen then get to object?
headline.expectedAnswer: The premise is wrong. The duty to prepare the closing numbers belongs to Buyer (Axogen, Inc.), not to the Stockholders’ Representative (Michelle Jarrard). Under Section 3.3(a), within ninety (90) days after the Closing Date Buyer must cause to be prepared and delivered to the Stockholders’ Representative the Closing Balance Sheet and Buyer’s calculations of Net Closing Working Capital, Transaction Expenses, Closing Indebtedness and Closing Cash. The objection right also runs the other way: under Section 3.3(c) the Stockholders’ Representative has forty-five (45) days after Buyer’s delivery to send a Notice of Objection; if she does not, Buyer’s calculations become final and binding. Axogen has no objection window of its own. After a Notice of Objection the two sides have thirty (30) days to resolve the Disputed Amounts before they may be submitted to an Independent Accountant.

Section 10.14 Backup Bidder.

If Buyer is not the winning bidder (or successful bidder) at any auction, but Buyer is the next highest or otherwise best bidder, Buyer may, in its sole discretion, elect to serve as a backup bidder (or “next highest or otherwise best bidder” or any similar designation) following any auction in accordance with the Bidding Procedures and Bidding Procedures Order.

Section 10.15 No Deposit.

Notwithstanding anything in this Agreement or the Bidding Procedures to the contrary, Buyer shall not be required to make any good faith deposit or similar deposit in connection with this Agreement or the Contemplated Transactions.
